steps.title: Step 2: Automatic project spots and the terrain rule (F37)
steps.plan: (a) Pure module town_bp/scripts/sites.js: the natural allow list (grass_block, dirt, coarse_dirt, podzol, mycelium, dirt_with_roots, mud, sand, red_sand, gravel, clay, stone, granite, diorite, andesite, deepslate, tuff, calcite, sandstone, red_sandstone, snow, snow_layer). Any block not on the list counts as man-made: planks, glass, cobblestone, terracotta, farmland, grass_path, crops, saplings, the lodestone, and anything a future update adds. Leaves count as natural only with persistent_bit false. A column with a log is a tree and is never cut. A solid block above an air gap rejects the spot (catches roofs and huts). The module also has the column model (N/W/T/M/L/U), the grading plan and the scoring. Grading: pad = median of the footprint's ground, then pad-1 and pad+1. Apron at distance d (1 or 2): t = pad + clamp(g - pad, -d, d). Cut or fill at most levelDepth (3). Steps between neighboring columns at most 1, the outside ring counted at its natural height. A cut column must not be next to water or lava, and the 2 blocks under each new top must be natural and solid. Filling uses dirt with the surrounding top block on top. Score in order: least leveling (in buckets of 6), already level, height variety (fewer picked pads within 1), distance (the well's counts 4 times). Docks go on the shoreline nearest the center, with 3x10 water. Every build faces the center. (b) Scan job: one town at a time, only while a player is within townRadius, a column cache, 12 column reads per tick, rings every 3 blocks, stop after 6 valid candidates once the next ring is 16 blocks past the best, then validate the best 3. Pending work is saved as t.scan. (c) Exclusions: one realm:claims_check for the whole town box (if it returns 10, check each finalist), realm:npc_places posts (6 blocks), the mayor (4), realm:place_ready story places (16, after realm:place_ping), other spots' regions (footprint + 2 must not overlap). Safe zones are not an exclusion (D4). (d) Placed-block cells: world.afterEvents.playerPlaceBlock marks 4x4x4 cells for natural kinds inside a town, stored in town:pl:<town>:0..1, at most 5,000 cells (when full: plf, and that town never levels). Also accept realm:blocks_placed {dim, box}. (e) Building at an automatic spot (Spot a:1, plan lv): show the outline to players within 32 for outlineSeconds, then validate block by block (and recheck claims; wait while a player stands on the spot; one rescan on failure). Save the snapshot over the whole region and its depth plus bs:1 before the first block. The build job does 48 block changes per tick and pauses on unloaded chunks. A build interrupted by a restart resumes from bs, and applying it twice changes nothing. Remove spot restores the terrain. (f) Menu: projects with no valid spot are listed in t.nos ('No good spot was found ... an operator can set one'), operators get a 'Find spots again' button, and spots operators set are kept and never leveled (D5). Existing towns get automatic spots for open and finished projects that have no spot.

steps.title: Step 4: Residents move in (F39)
steps.plan: (a) Gate D2 first, on BDS 1.26. Copy the vanilla villager_v2 behavior file (from the BDS 1.26 vanilla pack / Mojang's bedrock-samples) into town_bp/entities/villager_v2.json. Add one component group, realm:town_resident: minecraft:dweller with can_find_poi:false and can_migrate:false, plus minecraft:home with a restriction radius. Add one event, realm:become_resident. Base components stay unchanged so existing villagers are unaffected. Prove on BDS that a resident never claims a player's bed or job site and stays near home. If that cannot be proven, ship residents Disabled by default and report it. (b) Add town_bp to tools/sync-spawn.mjs (scripts/spawn.js). Spawn with spawnFresh(dim, 'minecraft:villager_v2', home, {spawnEvent:'minecraft:spawn_from_village', fresh:true}), then add the tags realm:resident, town:r:<town> and town:rid:<town>.<n>, a name from CONFIG.residentNames, the realm:become_resident event and the profession look event matching the house's job site. Save town:r:<town> {n, r:[{i,n,h,e,p,d}], new}. (c) Counts: residentsPerLevel [2,4,6,8,10]; level 1's two only once the well is built. Caps: residentCapTown 10 (config, hard limit) and residentCapWorld 20 (setting, 0-40). When over the world cap, serve the highest level first, then the oldest town. Lowering a cap never removes anyone. (d) Event driven: entityDie (entityTypes villager_v2) sets d = world.getAbsoluteTime() + replaceMinutes*1200. A census every 600 ticks, only for a town with a player in it, is one getEntities by tag: a resident missing twice while its home is loaded counts as gone; one past townRadius is teleported home; a duplicate rid loses its tags and is never killed. A due replacement spawns at its loaded home with 'A new family moved into <town>'. When a resident's home changes, it moves by respawning under the same name while nobody is within 24 blocks. (e) residentsTrade is Disabled by default: a beforeEvents.playerInteractWithEntity handler, whose first line is if (ev.cancel) return;, cancels taps on realm:resident.

decisions: D3 applied: new mayors start with the default NPC skin. An operator picks one in the NPC editor (sneak-tap in creative), and npc_bp's snapshot (realm_npc:m_<town>) keeps it.
D6 applied: Bram is never created, renamed or removed by town_bp. Move Bram here sends realm:npc_summon. When Bram is unplaced or far from every town, the oldest town is his.
D7 applied: mayors have roles ['mayor'] only. Affinity, gifts, keepsakes, talk points and Ask about are gated on folk.has(id) (the cast), and npc:aff never gets mayor keys.
D12: migration runs on the build interval as soon as a complete realm:npc_places answer is in, not inside a fixed 40-tick window. With no answer nothing is written. I corrected the design note.
D13: with townMayors Disabled, no mayors are made, asked for again or migrated. Mayors already standing stay, and every mayor-role NPC uses the int23 nearest-town rule.

D14: names are 'Mayor <first name>' from 20 mayorNames that do not clash with the cast, wanderers (wander_bp lines.js), elites or story characters (Pell, Tamsin, Jory, Nell and others were avoided). They show as 'Mayor Alda of Riverside' (mayorTemplate.title 'of {town}').

D15: town_bp does not save a mayor's post, because npc_bp owns posts. A mayor whose record is gone comes back at the town center facing south. A new mayor faces the way the operator faces, as /realm:npc_add does, instead of 'facing the operator'.

D16: /realm:npc_remove on a mayor also drops it from npc:mayors. With Town Projects it comes back with the default skin when a player is in its town, unless townMayors is Disabled. This is documented, and removing the town is the way to remove a mayor for good.
D17: a corrupt npc:mayors keeps every mayor: post and entity (the audit leaves them alone) until town_bp sets them again.
D18: mayors are left out of /realm:npc_houses and /realm:npc_add (the enum stays cast-only). They appear in Who lives here, /realm:npc_list and realm:npc_places, so the Minimap shows them.

items.summary: New pure module packs/town_bp/scripts/sites.js. It has the natural allow list (the 22 ids from the plan; anything else is man-made), UNDER (natural plus ores and bedrock) and WILD (main.js's PLANTS without air and sweet berry bush). Leaves are natural only with persistent_bit false; a log makes a column a tree. The column model readColumn gives N/W/T/M/L/U: a solid block over an air gap, or over a man-made block, is M; water is read through a surface() callback (C15); a missing read is U (C16). gradePlan: footprint at the pad, apron t = pad + clamp(g - pad, -d, d), at most levelDepth, steps of at most 1 against the outside ring at its natural height, and no water above the new top or lava next to a cut. The plan is saved as lv: outer x, inner z, '.' or '0'..'6'. scoreKey/compareKeys give the scoring order. scanTown is a generator that yields column, block and claims requests. Rings are every 3 blocks, from 6 for the well and 10 for the rest, out to radius-8. A project stops after 6 valid candidates once the next ring is 16 past the best, then the best 3 are deep-checked (2 UNDER blocks under every cut, plus a per-finalist claims check when 10 came back). Cheap rejects come before any read: radius-4, other regions (footprint+2), posts and places, claims. Placed cells are rejected per pad. The dock goes on the shore nearest the center, facing the water, with a 3x10 deck of the same surface and a margin of water or natural ground. Every other build has its front facing the center. Unknown columns make a project wait, unless `final`.

items.summary: New pure module packs/town_bp/scripts/placed.js holds the 4x4x4 cells relative to the town center, packed in 4 base-36 characters. They are saved in town:pl:<town>:0..1, 2,500 cells per property and 5,000 in all; past that the oldest are dropped and the town gets plf. items.summary: main.js wiring. t.scan (a list of project ids) is queued on add (as:1) and on level-up. Towns saved before this version queue once on the 100-tick check: current-level projects and finished projects without a spot (as:1). One scan at a time runs while a player is within townRadius (D10). It starts with a realm:claims_check over the town square (player "", 20-tick wait, no answer means no Land Claims), then sites.scanTown runs at 12 column or block reads a tick and at most 4,000 steps. Posts come from realm:npc_places (the town's mayor 4, others 6) and story places from realm:place_ready, with realm:place_ping sent at load+100 (16). Taken regions cover every spot in the dimension; pads are this town's spots. After 3 waiting scans in a session the scan becomes final. finishScan keeps picks that don't collide with a newly set operator spot. nos gets an ops message ('No good spot was found for Riverside's Well: an operator can set one'). A build at an a:1 spot is queued into a single budgeted job (a 1-tick interval, cleared when idle) instead of the one-tick build. The job goes through these steps: (1) outline for outlineSeconds to players within 32, with 'goes up here in N seconds'; (2) checkRegion, 32 reads a tick from pad-5 to top+1 over footprint+2: allowedInRegion, placed cells, ground within 3 of the plan, 2 UNDER blocks under every cut; (3) wait while a player is anywhere in the region ('Step off the spot'); (4) recheck claims; (5) snapshot of the whole region and its depth, then s.bs=1; (6) applyBuild at 48 steps a tick: cuts top-down remove only NATURAL and WILD blocks, fills bottom-up put dirt into open air right under the new top (never into a cave), the top block becomes lt (or grass on bared dirt), then the design through the new placeDesignSteps generator, where auto 'ground' places may replace natural ground. An unloaded chunk pauses the job and bs resumes it; a resumed job skips outline and check (D24). A failed check or snapshot calls respot: one rescan (rt), then nos. Remove spot and Relocate also take away a half-done build (bs), with kinds plus dirt and lt. restoreGround now runs two passes (air top-down, then the rest bottom-up). Menus: project lines read '(a spot is being picked)', '(no good spot was found: an operator can set one)' or '(being built)'. The town page lists nos lines. Operators get 'Find spots again' and a nos line in /realm:town, and Manage spots explains automatic spots. applySpot clears scan, nos and rt, so an operator spot is kept and never leveled (D5). The join reminder skips projects being scanned. New options autoSpots (Enabled), levelDepth (3, 0-3) and outlineSeconds (5, 0-15) are in config.js and settings.js. Test hooks: scan, build_pause{after}, and dump now has scanning, building, cells and regions. findings.problem: The scan's per-tick budget does not limit its pure-JS work. stepScan (main.js ~2115) only counts generator yields (SCAN_READS_TICK=12, SCAN_STEPS_TICK=4000), but scanTown yields only when a column is not in its cache. Candidates whose regions are already cached (house_2..house_N use the same 7x7 design as house_1, and later projects re-walk the rings house_1 read) run evalBuild + gradePlan for every ring position with no yield, all inside one tick. I measured it with a node harness on sites.js (scratchpad g5/spike.mjs: rolling natural terrain, radius 96, 4 houses): one gap between yields was 62-117 ms in V8. Bedrock's QuickJS is much slower, so a level-up that queues 4+ houses can stall the server for hundreds of ms in a single tick (watchdog / slow-script risk). This breaks section 10's "about 0.4 ms/tick" claim and the PACKS.md Cost text.
findings.fix: Count work, not yields: give scanTown a step counter (e.g. yield ["tick"] every N candidates, or after every evalBuild/gradePlan), and have stepScan treat that request as the end of its tick budget. Add a unit test that drives scanTown on cached terrain and checks the largest compute gap between yields (or the number of candidates evaluated between yields) stays bounded.

findings.problem: A resumed automatic build skips every safety check (stepBuild: phase = s.bs ? "apply" : ..., D24). There is no outline, no checkRegion, no 'step off the spot' wait (playersOn), no claims check, and placed cells marked since the first check are not looked at. A resume can happen long after the first check: the build pauses when its chunk unloads and resumes whenever a player comes within 64 blocks. Then: (a) applyBuild's cut sets any NATURAL/WILD block to air with no drop, so dirt, sand or stone a player placed on the half-leveled spot meanwhile, and flowers they planted, are deleted (playerPlaceBlock marked them, but nothing reads the marks on resume); (b) fills and the design (house walls, the well) are placed onto a player standing in the region, which can entomb or suffocate them; (c) for a config project with a saved `structure`, structureManager.place overwrites everything in its box, including a chest a player put there, so its contents are lost. D24's argument that only natural blocks are cut is true, but it ignores that players place natural-kind blocks and stand on spots.
findings.fix: On resume, still run the 'standing' phase. Also re-check the placed cells (touches(...)) over the region, and skip, or respot, columns where a mark is newer than the plan. For a structure build, re-validate its box block by block (or drop structure projects from automatic spots) before place().

findings.problem: Player-planted flowers and plants are never recorded as placed, so builds and paths remove them with no drop. The playerPlaceBlock handler (~2908) only marks NATURAL kinds ('anything else is man-made anyway'), but WILD plants (poppy, tulips, cornflower, mushrooms, ferns, pink_petals, leaf_litter, sunflower, lilac, rose_bush...) count as natural in the scan (readColumn skips them, allowedInRegion allows them). applyBuild's cut and placeDesignSteps replace them with setPermutation (no drop). A player's flower bed on open grass can therefore be chosen as a spot and wiped. In the same way, layPath clears a CLEARABLE flower on every path cell (setPermutation(air), no drop), and restoreLife turns the path back to grass without putting the flower back (the `c: 1` flag is saved but never used on restore).
findings.fix: Also mark WILD/CLEARABLE kinds in playerPlaceBlock (they are only placed by players or bonemeal), and have paths stop at flowers instead of clearing them, or restore the plant from `c` (and keep its id) on Remove spot.

items.summary: Review fix (high): scanTown now counts its own work. Each column lookup counts, cached or not, plus 8 and the list lengths per position. At SCAN.workTick = 400 it yields ["tick"], and stepScan ends its tick on it. So later houses that re-walk cached rings no longer evaluate every candidate in one tick. Measured with node --jitless, the closest stand-in for QuickJS here, on the reviewer's rolling-terrain harness (well plus 5 houses, radius 96): median 0.59 ms a tick, p99 2.1 ms, total 4,898 ticks. Before, single gaps were 62-117 ms even in JIT V8. The rare 7-8 ms outliers are GC: they fall at random ticks and also appear at workTick 300. The cost is that a level takes about 1 to 5 minutes to pick its spots. PACKS.md Cost and How to use, design note section 10 and D68 are updated. Scenario spot waits are raised from 2400 to 6000 ticks. town_bp is bumped to 1.7.1 and sync-diag was run.

items.summary: Review fix (medium): a resumed build (bs) now starts at 'standing', not 'apply'. It waits players off the spot, checks claims again, and keeps the existing snapshot. The apply phase also pauses while a player is in the region. applyBuild and placeDesignSteps take a `mine` predicate, which reads town:pl cells live. They never cut, fill or build over a block in a cell a player placed blocks in since the check, and apply waits while those cells are unreadable. Before structureManager.place, the structure's box is checked block by block: only unmarked air, natural ground or wild plants may be there. A claim over a half-done build, or a blocked structure box, holds the build (session map heldBuilds, one ops message). It does not respot, which would forget a half-leveled spot. Remove spot clears the hold, and a restart tries again. PACKS.md, D24 (corrected) and D69 are updated.
